**Allowed origins**

CORS is set in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It uses `app.use('*', cors({...}))` from `hono/cors`, with an `origin` callback at lines 21-31. The callback returns the request's origin if it matches one of these, and `null` otherwise:

- `http://localhost:4200`, as an exact match.
- Any origin ending in `.pages.dev`.
- Any origin ending in `.workers.dev`.

A request with no `Origin` header gets `null` (line 22). Browsers send `Origin` on cross-origin requests, so this affects non-browser clients, not browser callers.

The same block allows methods `GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS` and headers `Content-Type, Authorization`. It sets `maxAge` to 86400.

**Adding a custom domain**

Add a condition to the `if (...)` inside the `origin` function at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. For example, add `|| origin === 'https://app.example.com'`. Use the full origin: scheme, host and port, with no trailing slash. Use an exact match rather than `endsWith`, because `endsWith('example.com')` would also match `evil-example.com`.

Don't put the domain in an array. The comment at line 20 notes that Hono treats array entries as exact strings, and the origin callback exists to support the wildcard entries. `worker/src/index.md:24-25` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 say the same.

After editing, redeploy the Worker. I only read `worker/src/index.ts` and searched the `worker` directory. I didn't check whether the frontend has its own API base URL setting that also needs updating for the new domain.
